body:
The parent issue with description is #2690 

Proposed level changes for requirement in chapter "V53 WebRTC"

Full list of requirements for the chapter is listed here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x53-V53-WebRTC.md

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **53.1.1** | [ADDED] Verify that the Traversal Using Relays around NAT (TURN) service only allows access to IP addresses that are not reserved for special purposes (e.g., internal networks, broadcast, loopback). Note that this applies to both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. | 1 > 2 |
| **53.1.2** | [ADDED] Verify that the Traversal Using Relays around NAT (TURN) service is not susceptible to resource exhaustion when legitimate users attempt to open a large number of ports on the TURN server. | 2 > 3 |
| **53.2.1** | [ADDED] Verify that the key for the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) certificate is private by ensuring it is not reused in existing products or open-source projects and confirming it is not distributed or leaked. | 1 > 2 |
| **53.2.2** | [ADDED] Verify that the media server is configured to use and support strong and secure DTLS cipher suites and DTLS-SRTP protection profiles. | 1 > 2 |
| **53.2.3** | [ADDED] Verify that the media server is not susceptible to the "WebRTC DTLS ClientHello Race Condition" vulnerability by checking if the media server is publicly known to be vulnerable or by performing the race condition test. | 2 > 3 |
| **53.2.4** | [ADDED] Verify that Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) authentication is checked at the media server to prevent Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) injection attacks from leading to either a Denial of Service condition or audio or video media insertion into media streams. | 1 > 2 |
| **53.2.5** | [ADDED] Verify that the media server is able to continue processing incoming media traffic during a flood of Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) packets from legitimate users. | 2 > 3 |
| **53.2.6** | [ADDED] Verify that any audio or video recording mechanisms associated with the media server are able to continue processing incoming media traffic during a flood of Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) packets from legitimate users. | 2 > 3 |
| **53.2.8** | [ADDED] Verify that the DTLS certificate is checked against the SDP fingerprint attribute, terminating the media stream if the check fails, to ensure the authenticity of the media stream. | 1 > 3 |

comments.body:
> 53.2.8 [ADDED] Verify that the DTLS certificate is checked against the SDP fingerprint attribute, terminating the media stream if the check fails, to ensure the authenticity of the media stream.

Verification of the DTLS certificate is imprortant to guarantee the confidentiality of the WebRTC exchange. I'm not sure it is a good idea to have it in L3 (on the other hand, I would not expect this potential vulnerability to ever happen in practice (?)).

> on the other hand, I would not expect this potential vulnerability to ever happen in practice (?)

I think this is the key thing as to why it ends up as L3, because it is an unlikely issue in a niche area
